desc_en: Held every year in early February, centered on Odori Park, this is Sapporo's great winter celebration. Countless works line the venues, from towering giant snow sculptures to handmade pieces by local residents, and at night illumination gives them a magical glow. Don't miss the ice sculptures at the Susukino site either. Visitors arrive from across Japan and abroad, making this the liveliest season in snowy Sapporo.
quiz_en: The Sapporo Snow Festival began in 1950. What kind of people built the very first snow sculptures in Odori Park?

desc_en: This long, narrow park runs like a ribbon east to west for about 1.5 km through the heart of Sapporo. The Sapporo TV Tower stands at its eastern end, and flower beds, fountains and lawns stretch along its length. With lilacs in early summer, beer gardens in summer and the Snow Festival in winter, it hosts the city's seasonal events all year round and is a favorite place for locals to relax.
quiz_en: What is the name of the symbolic tower that stands at the eastern end of Odori Park, watching over the city of Sapporo?

desc_en: This local style of ramen was born in harsh, cold Sapporo. A rich miso broth with medium-thick wavy noodles, finished with stir-fried vegetables and lard to keep it from cooling, makes a bowl that warms you to the core on a snowy night. In Susukino there is a ramen alley packed with tiny shops, where you can see people hopping from one to the next.
quiz_en: What soup flavor, known for originating in Sapporo, spread the name of Sapporo ramen throughout Japan?

area_en: Kita Ward and Higashi Ward, Sapporo City; Ishikari City; Tobetsu Town
desc_en: Rising in the Daisetsuzan mountains, this great river nourishes the Kamikawa Basin and the Ishikari Plain before flowing into Ishikari Bay, and it is one of Hokkaido's most representative rivers. It is the third longest in Japan, after the Shinano and Tone rivers. It flows gently along the north side of Sapporo, with wide riverbanks and farmland around it. In autumn salmon swim upstream, and the river has long been closely tied to life along its banks.
quiz_en: Which fish swims up the Ishikari River in autumn and also stars in the local hot pot dish called Ishikari-nabe?

name_en: Beer and Jingisukan Lamb Barbecue at the Beer Garden
desc_en: At the beer garden in Sapporo's Higashi Ward, you can enjoy draft beer and jingisukan (grilled lamb) inside a red-brick building. The Hokkaido way is to grill the lamb on a distinctive dome-shaped pan while the vegetables around the edge cook almost as if simmering. The savory smoke rising up and the clink of beer mugs make for a lively evening on your trip.
quiz_en: The jingisukan pan rises like a little mountain in the middle. What clever purpose do you think that shape serves?

desc_en: This vast park was designed by sculptor Isamu Noguchi as "one single sculpture as a whole." On the site of a former waste disposal facility, the gently sloping Mount Moere, a glass pyramid, fountains and other features are arranged in geometric patterns. The grassy hills, which change their look with each season, are a place where you can feel the wide-open sky.
quiz_en: Who is the artist who designed Moerenuma Park so that the entire park would form one single sculpture?

name_en: Night View of Hakodate from Mount Hakodate
desc_en: From the summit of Mount Hakodate, the city's narrow waist, squeezed between the sea on both sides, appears as a glowing band of light. Around sunset, as the lights come on across town, you can enjoy both the ever-changing colors of the sky and the night view. The summit is easy to reach by ropeway, and the view is a classic part of any visit to Hakodate.
quiz_en: What means of transport do most people take up to the summit of Mount Hakodate to see the night view?

name_en: Motomachi and Suehirocho Historic Streets, Hakodate
desc_en: At the foot of Mount Hakodate, churches, Western-style mansions and houses blending Japanese and Western styles line the slopes leading down to the port. This historic townscape is designated an Important Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings. An exotic atmosphere has lingered since the port opened, and from the top of Hachiman-zaka slope you can take in the harbor and the sea. Stroll the cobbled slopes at leisure and feel the history of this port town.
quiz_en: What are the buildings called, common in Motomachi and Suehirocho, that have a Japanese-style ground floor and a Western-style second floor?

desc_en: This star-shaped Western-style fortress was built at the end of the Edo period. It is known as the stage for the final battle of the Boshin War, where former shogunate forces made their base, and the Hakodate Magistrate's Office has been reconstructed on the grounds. In spring, cherry trees along the moat outline the star, and from the neighboring Goryokaku Tower you can clearly look down on its shape.
quiz_en: What is the name of the final battle of the Boshin War, fought with the star-shaped Goryokaku as its stage?

desc_en: Japan's northernmost zoo became famous almost overnight for its "behavioral exhibits," which let you see animals' natural movements and abilities. You can get close to lively creatures, such as penguins that seem to fly as they swim underwater and seals gliding through a cylindrical tank. In winter, the zoo also holds walks in which penguins march in a line across the snow.
quiz_en: Which bird is the star of Asahiyama Zoo's winter walk, waddling in a single line through the snow?

desc_en: Kushiro Marsh and its surroundings are home to the red-crowned crane, a Special Natural Monument. Their numbers once fell to the brink of extinction but recovered thanks to conservation efforts such as feeding by local people. In winter you can watch their courtship dance, wings spread and calling to each other on the snowfields, their white and black plumage and red crowns standing out against the frozen landscape.
quiz_en: The top of a red-crowned crane's head looks red, but it is not red feathers. What are you actually seeing there?

desc_en: This group of lakes centers on Lake Akan, cradled by Mount Oakan and Mount Meakan. Lake Akan is known as a habitat of marimo, algae that grow into balls, and on its shore you will find a hot spring town and the Ainu Kotan, a village that passes on Ainu culture. The scenery of forests, volcanoes and calm waters is also well worth viewing from a sightseeing boat.
quiz_en: What is the round green alga that grows in Lake Akan and is designated a Special Natural Monument?

area_en: Kushiro City and nearby towns and villages
desc_en: Japan's largest marsh is a land of reeds and sedges through which the Kushiro River winds in great curves. In 1980 it became Japan's first wetland registered under the Ramsar Convention, and it has also been designated a national park. You can feel this grand nature with your whole body, whether gazing out from an observatory at marshland stretching to the horizon or paddling down the river by canoe.
quiz_en: In 1980, Kushiro Marsh became the first site in Japan registered under which international treaty for protecting wetlands?

name_en: Drift Ice of the Okhotsk Coast
desc_en: In winter, drift ice that has traveled from far to the north surges onto the Sea of Okhotsk coast, covering the sea in white. In Monbetsu you can board a sightseeing ship that breaks through the ice as it goes, experiencing the frozen sea up close. When the ice reaches the shore, even the creaking of the ice and the cold, clear air become lasting memories of your trip.
quiz_en: What is the name of the sightseeing icebreaker in Monbetsu that crushes drift ice with drill-like devices as it sails?

desc_en: This caldera lake, formed by volcanic eruptions, is known as Japan's northernmost lake that does not freeze. Its water is exceptionally clear, and on sunny days it turns a pure blue called "Shikotsu Blue." There are hot springs on the lakeshore, and in winter an ice festival using the lake's water is held. Its closeness to New Chitose Airport adds to the appeal of this quiet lake.
quiz_en: Which fish, known locally as "chippu," is a beloved specialty of Lake Shikotsu and familiar to everyone who visits the lake?

desc_en: In Jigokudani (Hell Valley), the remains of a volcanic explosion crater, steam and fumes rise everywhere and hot spring water gushes out. Noboribetsu Onsen (hot springs) is known for its many types of spring water, and comparing them as you hop between baths is part of the fun. Statues of oni (demons), inspired by Hell Valley, greet travelers all around town.
quiz_en: Inspired by Hell Valley, what kind of being appears as statues and characters all around the town of Noboribetsu Onsen?

desc_en: This lake was formed when an eruption of Hokkaido Komagatake dammed the area, and many islets large and small dot its surface. There are walking paths crossing the bridges between the islands as well as sightseeing boats, and the view of Komagatake across the lake is the signature scene of Onuma Quasi-National Park. Try strolling leisurely along the shore with some of the famous Onuma dango (rice dumplings) in hand.
quiz_en: What is the famous Onuma Park sweet in which dango dumplings, not on skewers, are packed into a folded wooden box?

desc_en: This active volcano rises on the Oshima Peninsula, and its shape changes dramatically depending on the direction you view it from. Seen from the Onuma side, its sharp peak is reflected in the lake, while from Shikabe Town on the sea side it appears grand, with its foothills spreading toward the ocean. Its slopes, marked by a history of eruptions, stand out on drives around Hakodate.
quiz_en: Hokkaido Komagatake looks very different depending on where you view it from. From which direction do you like its shape best?

desc_en: Called "Ezo Fuji" for its neat conical shape, this mountain is the symbol of the Shiribeshi region. In Kyogoku Town at its foot is a spring where snow and rain that fell on Mount Yotei emerge after many years as famously pure water, and many people come to draw it. Rising beyond the fields, the mountain makes a picture-perfect view in every season.
quiz_en: Because its beautiful shape closely resembles Mount Fuji, what nickname has been given to Mount Yotei?

desc_en: This wetland spreads out high on a mountain in the embrace of Mount Shokanbetsu. After hiking up a trail along a stream from the trailhead, you reach a marsh dotted with ponds large and small, where wetland plants bloom one after another from early summer through summer. Walking the boardwalks, you can savor a quiet landscape surrounded by mountains.
quiz_en: What are the small ponds that dot the Uryunuma Wetland, formed within the marsh itself, called?

desc_en: This gorge runs along the upper Ishikari River at the foot of the Daisetsuzan mountains, with cliffs of columnar joints rising like folding screens. The Ryusei (Shooting Star) and Ginga (Milky Way) waterfalls tumble from the cliffs, and in autumn the valley is colored by some of the earliest autumn leaves in Hokkaido. Sounkyo Onsen at the gorge's entrance is a busy base for exploring Daisetsuzan.
quiz_en: At Sounkyo, the Ryusei Falls and another waterfall flow side by side and are called the "married couple falls." What is the other one?

desc_en: Known as "the roof of Hokkaido," this group of mountains is the heart of Japan's largest mountain national park. A ropeway takes you partway up Asahidake, the highest peak, where alpine flowers bloom in summer and autumn leaves said to be the earliest in Japan spread in fall. The landscape of steaming slopes and lingering snow is something only this northern land can offer.
quiz_en: What is the name of the highest peak of the Daisetsuzan mountains, which is also the tallest mountain in Hokkaido?

name_en: Rural Landscape of the Biei Hills
desc_en: Gentle hills roll like waves, covered with colorful fields of wheat, potatoes, beans and other crops. The colors of the hills change with the seasons and crops, and lone trees standing here and there create picture-like scenes. The Tokachidake mountain range rises in the distance. The fields are farmers' important workplaces, so the golden rule is to enjoy the view from the road.
quiz_en: The scenery of colorful fields on the Biei Hills is often compared to the pattern of what kind of handicraft?

desc_en: This chain of volcanoes, with Mount Tokachidake as its main peak, still shows rugged slopes that send up volcanic smoke. Kamifurano Town at its foot is known for lavender fields that turn the hills purple in summer, and mountain hot springs such as Shirogane Onsen and Fukiage Onsen dot its slopes. The mountains lined up beyond the flower fields are a quintessential Furano view.
quiz_en: What flower turns the summer hills of Kamifurano Town, at the foot of the Tokachidake range, purple?

area_en: Otoineppu Village, Nakagawa Town, Teshio Town and Horonobe Town
desc_en: Rising in the Kitami Mountains, this river flows north across the land of northern Hokkaido into the Sea of Japan and is the second longest river in Hokkaido. With few dams, its gentle current is popular for canoe trips. Wilderness and pastures spread along its banks, and from Teshio Town at the river mouth you can see Rishiri Fuji floating across the sea.
quiz_en: From near the mouth of the Teshio River, "Rishiri Fuji" can be seen floating across the Sea of Japan. On which island is it?

desc_en: This vast wetland along the Sea of Japan is part of Rishiri-Rebun-Sarobetsu National Park. In early summer, wetland flowers bloom one after another, and as you walk the boardwalks, Mount Rishiri appears under the wide sky beyond the horizon. The scenery of this almost untouched wilderness has a scale found only in Japan's northernmost region.
quiz_en: Which flower, representative of Hokkaido's wetlands, turns the Sarobetsu Plain a vivid orange color in early summer each year?

name_en: Alpine Plant Communities of Rebun Island
desc_en: On Rebun Island, called "the floating island of flowers," flowers that on Honshu grow only high in the mountains bloom even in low places near the coast. It is a plant world unique to the island, shaped by harsh winds and cold. The flowers are at their best from early summer through summer, and you can enjoy them while hiking trekking courses that overlook the sea.
quiz_en: Which member of the orchid family grows wild only on Rebun Island and bears cream-colored, pouch-shaped flowers?

desc_en: Rishiri Island is almost entirely made up of a single mountain, and its peak is Mount Rishiri, also called "Rishiri Fuji." Its form, rising straight up from the sea, can be seen from surrounding islands and the opposite shore. The island's rich waters are known for producing kombu kelp and sea urchin, so seafood is as much a part of the trip as climbing.
quiz_en: What seaweed, a specialty of Rishiri Island, is famous throughout Japan as an ingredient for making dashi soup stock?

desc_en: This solitary peak rises solidly at the base of the Shiretoko Peninsula. Standing beyond the wide fields of Shari Town, it is the town's symbol. Part of the trail follows a stream lined with a series of waterfalls, and climbers love it as a mountain where you head for the summit to the sound of rushing water. From the top you can see the Sea of Okhotsk and the Shiretoko mountains.
quiz_en: Mount Shari rises beyond the fields of Shari Town. In which season would you most like to see it, and why?

desc_en: Five lakes are scattered through the primeval forest at the foot of the Shiretoko mountains. Mountains reflected on the water make this one of Shiretoko's signature views. The elevated boardwalk offers easy access, while the ground-level trails are walked with a guide during the season when brown bears are active. These are walking paths worthy of a World Natural Heritage site, where you can sense the presence of wildlife.
quiz_en: In what year was Shiretoko, which includes the Shiretoko Five Lakes, registered as a World Natural Heritage site?

area_en: Shari Town, Shibetsu Town and Rausu Town
desc_en: Tall cliffs line the coast of the Shiretoko Peninsula, and in some places waterfalls pour straight into the sea. The tip of the peninsula cannot be reached by land, so viewing it from a sightseeing boat is the standard way, and with luck you may spot brown bears walking along the shore. On the Rausu side, boats also head out to watch whales, orcas and dolphins.
quiz_en: What large black-and-white marine animal can sometimes be encountered from watching boats in the sea off Rausu?

desc_en: This caldera lake was formed by volcanic activity, with Nakajima Island floating at its center. To the south are Mount Usu and Showa-Shinzan, letting you feel up close how this land lives alongside volcanoes. At Toyako Onsen on the lakeshore, fireworks are launched over the lake almost every night from spring to autumn, a treat to enjoy after a soak.
quiz_en: What is the name of the volcano near Lake Toya that was born during wartime when a wheat field swelled up from the ground?

desc_en: This wetland spreads across Hamanaka Town, facing the Pacific Ocean, and is also called "the wetland of flowers" because flowers bloom in profusion here in summer. As its name suggests, sea fog often drifts in, and the dreamlike scenery shrouded in mist is part of its charm. From the observatory you can take in the wetland, the sea and scattered ponds all at once, and boardwalks let you explore at a relaxed pace.
quiz_en: At Kiritappu Wetland, which scenery did you encounter: a day wrapped in fog, or a clear and sunny one?

desc_en: This caldera lake is surrounded by steep cliffs, with no rivers flowing in or out. Its clarity ranks among the highest in the world, and on clear days the surface turns a deep blue called "Mashu Blue." It is often wrapped in fog and is also known as "foggy Lake Mashu." Visitors cannot go down to the water and instead view it from observatories.
quiz_en: What is the name of the small island that floats all alone in the deep blue waters of Lake Mashu?

desc_en: Japan's largest caldera lake has hot springs bubbling up all around its shores. At Sunayu, digging into the beach sand releases hot water, so you can make your own footbath. In winter swans fly in, and the view of the lake from Bihoro Pass above is magnificent. Circling the lake lets you experience the charms of eastern Hokkaido, blessed with volcanoes and hot springs.
quiz_en: At Sunayu on Lake Kussharo, what happens when you dig into the sand by the water's edge with your hands?

desc_en: This is the site of a large Jomon-period settlement where people are known to have lived over a long period. A large pillar-supported building made with huge chestnut-wood posts and a large pit dwelling have been reconstructed, letting you experience the scale of a Jomon village. It is registered as a World Heritage site as one of the Jomon Prehistoric Sites in Northern Japan, covering Hokkaido and northern Tohoku.
quiz_en: How many thick chestnut-wood pillars in total were used in the reconstruction of the large pillar-supported building at the Sannai-Maruyama Site?

name_en: Sukayu Onsen Hiba Wood Sennin-buro Bath
desc_en: This single-inn hot spring retreat for therapeutic bathing sits at about 900 m on the slopes of the Hakkoda Mountains. Its famous "Hiba Sennin-buro" (thousand-person bath) is a spacious, pillar-free great bath built entirely of hiba cypress, brimming with milky, acidic water. In winter it is buried in deep snow, and many people come to soak while gazing at the snow and breathing the mountain air.
quiz_en: In 1954, Sukayu Onsen, along with Shima and Nikko Yumoto, became one of Japan's first places designated as what?

desc_en: This group of volcanoes rises south of Aomori City, with more than ten peaks lined up and Mount Odake as the highest. Take the ropeway to the summit park for marshes, alpine plants and views reaching as far as Mutsu Bay. In autumn, beech and rowan trees color the mountains, and in winter they become peaks of heavy snow. The area is also known as the site of a tragic snow march accident in the Meiji era.
quiz_en: What is the title of the novel by Jiro Nitta that depicts the tragedy of the snow march on the Hakkoda Mountains?

name_en: Snow Monsters (Rime-Covered Trees) of the Hakkoda Mountains
desc_en: In midwinter on Hakkoda, snow and ice carried by strong seasonal winds cling thickly to the conifers, and rime-covered trees called "snow monsters" fill the mountainside. Ride the ropeway up near the summit and you enter another world lined with white monsters. On clear days, the contrast between the blue sky and pure white makes for a dazzling view.
quiz_en: What is the name of the conifer that forms the core of the Hakkoda snow monsters, wrapped in snow and ice?

desc_en: The Moya Highlands, a short drive from central Aomori, are a ski area loved by residents in winter. In autumn, cosmos flowers bloom across the slopes, and a festival is held to enjoy the flower fields swaying in the highland breeze. Looking down through the flowers from the top of the slope to Aomori City and Mutsu Bay is another pleasure unique to this place.
quiz_en: Standing among the cosmos on the Moya Highlands slopes, what view would you most like to look out over toward Aomori City?

desc_en: Rising tall above the Tsugaru Plain, this is the highest peak in Aomori Prefecture, called "Tsugaru Fuji" for its beautiful shape. Revered since ancient times as a sacred mountain, it has Iwakiyama Shrine at its foot. Apple orchards spread across its lower slopes, and seeing Mount Iwaki beyond white blossoms in spring or red fruit in autumn is a scene that symbolizes Tsugaru.
quiz_en: Mount Iwaki is the highest mountain in Aomori Prefecture. What nickname was it given for the beauty of its shape?

desc_en: Hirosaki Park, centered on Hirosaki Castle, is planted with many cherry trees such as Somei-Yoshino and is known as one of Japan's foremost cherry blossom spots. The Edo-period keep with cherries in full bloom and flowers reflected in the moats make a splendid sight. As the blossoms fall, the surface of the outer moat is covered in petals, creating what looks like a pink ribbon.
quiz_en: What is the name for the scene in which fallen cherry petals completely cover the outer moat of Hirosaki Park?

desc_en: This plateau spreads out above the Hyakuzawa area on the southeastern slopes of Mount Iwaki. Its open views down over the Tsugaru Plain and apple orchards below are a major attraction, and you can enjoy something different each season, from drives and walks through the greenery in summer to skiing on snowy slopes in winter. It is also a place where you can feel the sheer size of Mount Iwaki looming close.
quiz_en: Looking down on the Tsugaru Plain from the Iwaki Highlands, in which season, with which colors, would you like to visit?

desc_en: Located at the southeastern foot of Mount Iwaki, this shrine has long drawn the faith of the people of Tsugaru. Beyond an approach lined with cedar trees stand a vermilion-lacquered tower gate and richly painted shrine buildings, so splendid they are even called "Oku-Nikko." Mount Iwaki rises behind the shrine, letting you sense a faith that worships the mountain itself.
quiz_en: What is the traditional Tsugaru event, held in the eighth month of the old lunar calendar, in which people climb from Iwakiyama Shrine to the summit to worship?

desc_en: Kabushima, on the coast of Hachinohe City, is designated a national Natural Monument as a breeding ground for black-tailed gulls. From spring to summer the island is covered with gulls, and you can watch them raising their chicks up close. Kabushima Shrine sits atop the island, making it a unique place where you pray surrounded by the birds' noisy cries.
quiz_en: On Kabushima, being hit by gull droppings is said to bring good luck. What kind of Japanese wordplay is that saying based on?

desc_en: Ne Castle in Hachinohe City is the site of a castle built by the Nanbu clan during the Nanboku-cho period and is designated a national Historic Site. The main hall, workshops and other buildings have been reconstructed in the main enclosure, giving a feel for how medieval samurai lived. The festival held at this historic site is a local event that brings the history of Hachinohe's castle closer to home.
quiz_en: Who is the Nanboku-cho period warrior regarded as the founder of the Hachinohe Nanbu clan, who built Ne Castle in Hachinohe?

desc_en: This mountain lies in the hills of Nango Ward in Hachinohe City. Nango is a peaceful countryside area of fields and forests, and from the mountain you can look out over the villages below and toward Hachinohe. It is ideal for those who want to walk quiet mountain paths and enjoy nature in the seasons of fresh greenery or autumn leaves. It is a simple, rustic mountain landscape cherished by local people.
quiz_en: After a countryside walk in Nango Ward, Hachinohe, what local food would you like to enjoy once you come down the mountain?

desc_en: This temple stands in the forest of Mount Kuromori on the outskirts of Kuroishi City. Its grounds, surrounded by trees, are quiet, and you can take your time to pray while breathing in the mountain air. In central Kuroishi, a townscape remains with "komise," wooden arcades that shelter pedestrians from snow and sun, so you can enjoy the calm atmosphere of this old castle town together with the temple.
quiz_en: What are the wooden arcades that remain along the streets of Kuroishi, built to shelter people from snow and sunlight, called?

desc_en: This cherry blossom festival is held at Ashino Park in Kanagi, Goshogawara City. The park is planted with many cherry trees, and the stretch along the Tsugaru Railway line running through it becomes like a tunnel of blossoms. You can also enjoy strolling by the lake. Kanagi is the hometown of writer Osamu Dazai, and many people visit his birthplace, "Shayokan," as well.
quiz_en: Which writer was born in Kanagi, and has his family home open to the public as the "Shayokan"?

desc_en: This brackish lake on the Sea of Japan side of the Tsugaru Peninsula is where seawater and fresh water mix. The lake is known for its shijimi clams, and on the shore you can taste shijimi ramen and shijimi miso soup. In medieval times, a port town called Tosaminato flourished beside this lake. The hour when the sunset colors the lake and the Sea of Japan is especially memorable.
quiz_en: What is the proper species name of the clam that is Lake Jusan's specialty, used in shijimi ramen and shijimi soup?

desc_en: On the border of Aomori and Akita, this double caldera lake was formed by volcanic activity. Holding deep, clear water, it is, together with the Oirase Stream that flows out of it, the signature scenic spot of Towada-Hachimantai National Park. At Yasumiya on the lakeshore stands the "Statue of Maidens" by Kotaro Takamura, and in autumn the mountains surrounding the lake are dyed in fall colors.
quiz_en: Who was the sculptor and poet who created the "Statue of Maidens," the two facing figures that stand at Yasumiya on Lake Towada?

desc_en: This single-inn onsen (hot spring) near the Oirase Stream is surrounded by beech forest. Its water bubbles up straight through the gaps in the floorboards at the bottom of the tub, so you can enjoy fresh water that never touches the air. Nearby, walking paths circle Tsuta Pond and other ponds, and the forest is especially beautiful in the seasons of fresh green and autumn leaves.
quiz_en: Which writer of the Meiji and Taisho eras spent his final years at Tsuta Onsen and is known for his love of this place?

name_en: Mount Osorezan Sacred Site and Bathhouses
desc_en: This sacred site spreads along the shore of Lake Usori in the mountains of the Shimokita Peninsula. Its rocky ground, filled with the smell of sulfur, is likened to hell, while the white sand beach and blue lake are likened to the Pure Land paradise. Counted among Japan's three great sacred sites, it also has simple bathhouses on its grounds that worshippers may use. Its otherworldly stillness lingers in the heart.
quiz_en: What are the women called who perform "kuchiyose," relaying the words of the dead, and who are known for appearing at the Osorezan grand festival?

desc_en: This cherry blossom festival is held in Mutsu City on the Shimokita Peninsula, at the northern edge of Honshu. Cherries in the north bloom later than in most parts of Honshu, reaching their peak when blossoms at other famous spots have already given way to leaves. When the flowers bloom together in this town after the long winter, people gather beneath them to celebrate the long-awaited arrival of spring.
quiz_en: If you visited the cherry blossom festival in Mutsu City, what Shimokita Peninsula specialty would you want to enjoy along with the flowers?

desc_en: This hot spring lies in the forest of Mount Yatate, in the hills beyond Tanabu in central Mutsu City. It is wrapped in the deep woods typical of the Shimokita Peninsula, so you can soak at leisure in quiet surroundings. It is perfect for a stop on a trip around Shimokita's mountain sights, such as Osorezan and the Yagen Gorge, to soothe tired legs after a hike.
quiz_en: After a soak in Mutsu Yatate Onsen, a mountain hot spring of Shimokita, which famous Shimokita spot would you like to visit next?

desc_en: This hot spring is in the Sekine area of Mutsu City. Sekine faces the Tsugaru Strait, and travelers are greeted by sea breezes and the simple scenery of Shimokita. After soaking in waters loved by local people and easing the fatigue of your journey, gaze along the coastline on a clear day and see whether you can spot the land of Hokkaido across the strait.
quiz_en: On a clear day, from the seaside at Sekine in Mutsu City facing the Tsugaru Strait, what land can be seen across the water?

desc_en: Located on the grounds of a hotel in Tanabu, Mutsu City, this hot spring is an easy in-town stop. The name "Tonami" comes from the Tonami Domain, established in this area in the early Meiji era by people who moved here after their defeat in the Boshin War. You can take a relaxing soak while reflecting on the history of those who carved out a new life in a harsh environment.
quiz_en: In the early Meiji era, people moved to the area around Mutsu City and founded the Tonami Domain. Which domain had they come from?

desc_en: This hot spring village bubbles up along the upper Kawauchi River in the mountains of Kawauchi, Mutsu City. Surrounded by deep forest, it is a quiet spa village where you can soak while listening to the murmur of the stream. The Kawauchi River valley is beautiful with autumn leaves, and it is best visited along with a drive or a walk. Its rustic simplicity, fitting for a secluded retreat of Shimokita, is its charm.
quiz_en: While soaking at Yunokawa Onsen Village along the Kawauchi River stream, what sounds did you hear around you?

desc_en: This wetland spreads across the plains of Tsugaru City, where wetland flowers bloom one after another from early summer through summer. Ponds large and small dot the surroundings, and the open view of Mount Iwaki across the marsh is another draw. Walking the boardwalk built through the wetland, you can feel the rich waterside nature of the Tsugaru Plain up close.
quiz_en: What is the name of the flower in the lily family that covers Bense Wetland in a carpet of yellow in early summer?

desc_en: This park spreads along the shore of a pond in the Kizukuri area of Tsugaru City. Amid the greenery around the water, it is a local place to relax with walks and seasonal flowers. Tsugaru City is known for the Jomon-period Kamegaoka Site, and at JR Kizukuri Station a giant station building shaped like a shakoki dogu clay figure welcomes travelers.
quiz_en: What type of clay figure, associated with the Kamegaoka Site, is the JR Kizukuri Station building in Tsugaru City shaped like?

desc_en: This grand festival is held at Saruka Shrine in Hirakawa City around the time of the autumn harvest moon. The shrine has long been beloved by the people of Tsugaru, and a lotus pond spreads across its grounds. On festival days the precincts bustle with worshippers and food stalls, and together with the moon floating in the clear autumn night sky, it has become a seasonal tradition of autumn in Tsugaru.
quiz_en: On the night of the harvest moon festival, what autumn offering would you like to eat while gazing up at the moon?

desc_en: This single-inn hot spring lies deep in the mountains of Ikarigaseki in Hirakawa City. It boasts an abundant flow, and its bath, where water overflows from the tub and runs across the floor, lets you feel the power of the spring. In the mountain stillness you can savor the atmosphere of a rustic therapeutic spa. It is in the hills near the Akita border, and some people visit during a drive.
quiz_en: At Kotobe Onsen, a single inn deep in the mountains, what did you feel as you watched the water overflowing from the bath?

desc_en: This hot spring is in Ikarigaseki, Hirakawa City, near the Akita border. Ikarigaseki was a key transportation point where the Tsugaru Domain placed a checkpoint in the Edo period, and today a reconstructed checkpoint gate at the roadside station conveys the atmosphere of those days. Inns are scattered along the Hirakawa River, and like travelers of old, you can rest in a hot spring on the highway.
quiz_en: What facility, still remembered in the place name Ikarigaseki, did the Tsugaru Domain set up here during the Edo period?

desc_en: This hot spring is in Hiranai Town, facing Mutsu Bay. Hiranai is known as a town where scallop farming thrives, and along the coast there are places to enjoy scallop dishes. In winter, swans fly in to the Asadokoro coast on the Natsudomari Peninsula. After warming up in waters loved by local people, go and take in the calm scenery of Mutsu Bay.
quiz_en: Which shellfish, representative of Aomori, is widely farmed along the shores of Mutsu Bay, including in Hiranai Town?

desc_en: This hot spring is in Yomogita Village, facing Mutsu Bay on the east side of the Tsugaru Peninsula. The village is a land of peaceful scenery lying between the sea and farmland. It is also loved by locals as a day-trip bath, a place to catch your breath during your travels. After your bath, try walking the quiet seaside, where you can see the Natsudomari Peninsula and the Shimokita mountains across Mutsu Bay.
quiz_en: In Yomogita Village on Mutsu Bay, which view would you rather enjoy after your bath: the sea or the rice paddies?

desc_en: This park sits on a small hill near the center of Kanita in Sotogahama Town, looking down over Mutsu Bay. Cherry trees bloom in spring, and from the hilltop you can see the sea and the town, and on clear days all the way to the Shimokita Peninsula across the bay. Kanita appears in Osamu Dazai's travel writing about his journey around Tsugaru, and many people come to visit this literary setting.
quiz_en: What is the title of the travelogue-style novel Osamu Dazai wrote after traveling through Kanita and other towns of his home region, Tsugaru?

desc_en: This hot spring rises in the highlands of Ajigasawa Town at the northwestern foot of Mount Iwaki. The surroundings form a highland resort with a ski area and golf course, and from the heights you can look out over the Sea of Japan and the Tsugaru countryside. Its charm is soaking in the embrace of Mount Iwaki, after snow play in winter or in the cool highland breeze in summer.
quiz_en: At Ajigasawa Kogen Onsen at the foot of Mount Iwaki, which would you choose to visit: the snowy season or the green season?

desc_en: This grand festival is held at Shirahachimangu Shrine in Ajigasawa, a port town facing the Sea of Japan. The shrine has long drawn the faith of the townspeople, and during the festival processions with mikoshi (portable shrines) parade through town while spectators crowd the streets. It is a festival where you can feel the history of a port that prospered with the Kitamae trading ships and the spirit of people who live alongside the sea.
quiz_en: After watching the mikoshi procession at the Shirahachimangu Grand Festival in the port town of Ajigasawa, what local seafood flavor would you want to try?

desc_en: This hot spring lies near the center of Ajigasawa Town, facing the Sea of Japan. As befits a seaside town, in the evening the sun sinking into the Sea of Japan turns the sky red. Ajigasawa is a port town known for seafood such as grilled dried squid, and if you stroll the beach after your bath, you can feel the atmosphere of a Tsugaru fishing town along with the sea breeze.
quiz_en: In Ajigasawa Town, an Akita dog became a nationwide star after its "ugly-cute" face drew attention. What is the dog's name?

desc_en: This historic temple stands in the port town of Fukaura, facing the Sea of Japan. Fukaura prospered as a port where Kitamae ships waited for favorable winds, and the temple drew the faith of sailors praying for safe voyages. Many ship ema votive paintings offered by sailors have been handed down here, along with topknots cut off and dedicated in gratitude by people saved from shipwrecks. It is a temple alive with the prayers of seafaring people.
quiz_en: What are the votive pictures called, many of which remain at Enkaku-ji, that Kitamae ship sailors offered to pray for safe voyages?

desc_en: This is the coast of a cape jutting into the Sea of Japan in Fukaura Town. The top of the cape is open grassland, while rugged reefs stretch below the cliffs. Because the view opens wide toward the sea, it becomes a perfect spot in the evening to watch the sun sink into the Sea of Japan. You can enjoy the grand ocean scenery typical of the Gono Line area.
quiz_en: Standing atop Yukiaizaki cape jutting into the Sea of Japan and watching the sunset, what came to your mind?

desc_en: At the western foot of the Shirakami Mountains, many lakes and ponds large and small are scattered through the beech forest. Among them, Aoike (Blue Pond) is known for its translucent blue, as if ink had been poured in, and its mysterious color amazes visitors. Following the forest trails around the ponds, you can fully appreciate the beauty of Shirakami's beech woods and clear water.
quiz_en: Among the Juniko lakes, what is the name of the pond famous for its mysterious blue color, as if ink had been poured into it?

desc_en: This coast of broad rock shelves was formed when the seabed was uplifted by a great earthquake in the Edo period. Its name is known to come from a feudal lord who held a banquet here after laying tatami mats on the rocks. The Gono Line runs right alongside, so the scenic spot can be seen from the train window too. The hour when the sun setting into the Sea of Japan lights the rocks red is especially memorable.
quiz_en: As the origin of the name Senjojiki Coast, what is the lord of Tsugaru said to have spread on these rocks to hold a banquet?

desc_en: This coast lies at the southern tip of Fukaura Town, near the border with Akita Prefecture. The Shirakami Mountains press right up to the Sea of Japan, and a simple seaside landscape of rocks and small beaches unfolds. From the Gono Line and the national highway running along the coast, you can enjoy broad views of the Sea of Japan, making it a memorable place as the gateway into or out of Aomori.
quiz_en: At Omagoshi Coast, caught between the Shirakami mountains and the Sea of Japan, what color was the sea you saw there?

desc_en: This rocky coast stretches along the Sea of Japan in Fukaura Town. The Gono Line runs right nearby, and the combination of trains running along the very edge of the shoreline and the rough Sea of Japan is one of the line's most representative views. At dusk, the sun sinking below the horizon lights up the rocks, and time flows with a strong sense of travel.
quiz_en: On the Gono Line running along Kasose Coast, would you rather watch the rough Sea of Japan from the train window or from the shore?

name_en: Beech Forests of the Shirakami Mountains
desc_en: In the Shirakami Mountains straddling the Aomori-Akita border, one of the world's largest virgin beech forests remains, almost untouched by human hands. It was registered as a World Natural Heritage site as a forest nurturing diverse plants and animals. The forest changes its look with the seasons, from bright green in spring to gold in autumn, and the more you walk, the more you feel its depth.
quiz_en: In what year were the Shirakami Mountains, together with Yakushima, registered as Japan's first World Natural Heritage sites?

desc_en: These waterfalls in the Anmon Gorge of Nishimeya Village, on the eastern side of the Shirakami Mountains, consist of three falls in a series of steps. The falls that appear after you follow the streamside path through the beech forest are truly powerful. Parts of the trail run right beside the stream, and you head for the falls feeling both the harshness and beauty of nature with your whole body.
quiz_en: Walking through the beech forest to Anmon Falls, which moved you more: the forest along the way or the waterfalls themselves?

desc_en: Located in the middle of the Tsugaru Plain, Itayanagi is an "apple town" with orchards spreading throughout. In spring, white blossoms adorn the orchards, and in autumn the trees are heavy with red fruit. Mount Iwaki rises beyond the orchards, and the scenery created by apple trees and the mountain is unique to Tsugaru. You can enjoy a different look in every season.
quiz_en: Apples grow in the orchards of Itayanagi and across Aomori. What color are the apple blossoms that bloom there in spring?

desc_en: This cherry blossom festival is held in spring in Tohoku Town, on the shore of Lake Ogawara. As the late spring of northern Tohoku arrives, people gather beneath the cherries in full bloom. Tohoku Town faces Lake Ogawara, the largest lake in Aomori Prefecture, and is also known for the lake's bounty, such as shijimi clams and wakasagi smelt. You can enjoy the lakeside scenery along with the blossoms.
quiz_en: What is the name of the largest lake in Aomori Prefecture, known for shijimi clams and smelt, that Tohoku Town faces?

desc_en: This park lies in the lush green hills of Oirase Town. With walking paths and open spaces, it is a place for local people to relax, strolling while enjoying seasonal flowers and the greenery of the trees. Oirase is a town on the plains near the Pacific Ocean, and its name comes from a river that flows through the town.
quiz_en: What is the name of the river, flowing from Lake Towada to the Pacific Ocean, that gave Oirase Town its name?

desc_en: On the western coast of the Shimokita Peninsula, this scenic spot features sharp, whitish-green rocks towering upward. Strange rock formations carved by wind and waves over many years continue for about 2 km, lined with rocks likened to figures of the Buddha. The standard ways to get there are to descend a walking path from the road or to approach from the sea on a sightseeing boat from Sai or Wakinosawa.
quiz_en: What type of whitish-green rock makes up the strange, Buddha-like rock formations that line the Hotokegaura coast?

desc_en: This park is in the Yagoshi area of Sai Village on the west coast of the Shimokita Peninsula, facing the Tsugaru Strait. Rocks carved by rough waves line the shore, and there are open views of Hokkaido across the strait. Sai Village is where sightseeing boats depart for Hotokegaura, and it is a place to enjoy the western Shimokita coastline woven from cliffs and sea.
quiz_en: Looking at the Tsugaru Strait from the seaside of Sai Village, what land can be seen on the far shore on a clear day?

desc_en: This hot spring rises in the hills of Gonohe Town, in a highland area with ranches. Peaceful pastures spread around it, and you can relax in the bath amid open scenery. Gonohe has deep ties with horses, and horse meat dishes are cherished as a local taste. After your bath, be sure to seek out some of the local flavors.
quiz_en: What is the hot pot dish of simmered horse meat called, cherished as a local taste in Gonohe and the Nanbu region?

desc_en: This hot spring is beside a river in the Kuraishi area of Gonohe Town. Kuraishi is a quiet district surrounded by fields and mountains, and the bath is loved by local people for day visits. The area is also known for beef cattle, including a brand of beef named after the place. Wrapped in the peaceful countryside scenery of the Nanbu region, you can take a leisurely soak.
quiz_en: After a rest at the hot spring in Kuraishi, Gonohe Town, what local Nanbu region specialty would you like to taste?

desc_en: This waterfall in the mountains of Takko Town shows water cascading down the rock face in steps. It is surrounded by deep forest, and in the seasons of fresh greenery and autumn leaves the contrast between the falls and the colors of the trees is superb. Takko is a mountain town near the borders of Iwate and Akita, known throughout Japan as a producer of its specialty, garlic.
quiz_en: Takko Town, home of Miroku Falls, is known nationwide as one of Japan's leading producers of which specialty vegetable?

desc_en: This coast faces the Pacific Ocean in Hashikami Town, just south of Hachinohe City. Reefs and small coves continue along the shore, creating a seaside landscape with pleasant sea breezes and the sound of waves. In the morning, the sun rising from the Pacific lights up the sea, a view only early-rising travelers get to see. It is a simple yet powerful coast, fitting as the northern gateway to the Sanriku seas.
quiz_en: At Hashikami Coast facing the Pacific, which would you like to see: the sea glowing at sunrise, or the blue sea at midday?

desc_en: This mountain rises in Hashikami Town near the Aomori-Iwate border. With its gentle shape and well-maintained trails, it is a hiking mountain beloved by locals. From near the summit you can see the Pacific Ocean, the streets of Hachinohe and, on clear days, distant mountains. Its appeal is that you can climb it casually while enjoying seasonal flowers and autumn leaves.
quiz_en: When you looked down on the Pacific Ocean from the summit of Mount Hashikami, what was the first thing that caught your eye?

desc_en: This is a festival of the Kannon (Goddess of Mercy) in the Terashita area of Hashikami Town. Terashita Kannon is a sacred site long revered by local people, and its grounds, surrounded by cedar groves, have a solemn atmosphere. On the festival day many worshippers visit, and local traditions are carried on. It is an important once-a-year day when the quiet mountain village comes alive.
quiz_en: At the annual festival of Terashita Kannon, surrounded by cedar groves, what would you like to ask of the Kannon?

desc_en: This hot spring lies in the hills of Shingo Village, east of Lake Towada. Shingo is a village of highland ranches, famous for milk and ice cream from Jersey cows. It is also known for a mysterious legendary site within the village called "the Tomb of Christ." At this quiet mountain village hot spring, you can spend relaxing, unhurried time.
quiz_en: Among sweets made with milk from Jersey cows, a famous specialty of Shingo Village, which one would you like to eat?

desc_en: A signature local dish of Iwate, wanko soba is served bite-sized, with a server tossing helping after helping of soba noodles into your bowl to cries of "hai, janjan!" The more you eat, the higher the empty bowls pile up, and the rule is that you close the lid yourself when you are full. At restaurants in Morioka you can enjoy it with condiments and side dishes amid lively calls.
quiz_en: When eating wanko soba, what do you do to your bowl to say "I'm full, thank you for the meal"?

desc_en: This dam lake lies in the hills of Tamayama Ward, northeast of Morioka City, surrounded by quiet forest. The area is known as one of the coldest places in Honshu, and in winter the lake surface freezes thickly. Ice fishing for wakasagi, cutting holes in the frozen lake, is a winter highlight, and colorful tents line up across the ice.
quiz_en: What is the name of the small fish that people catch through holes cut in the frozen surface of Lake Gando in winter?

desc_en: This summer festival is held on the shores of Lake Gosho, created by damming the Shizukuishi River west of Morioka City. The surroundings have been developed into a large park, busy with families spending time on the lakeside lawns and by the water. Beyond the lake rises the stately Mount Iwate, and at summer dusk the lake and mountain take on beautiful colors.
quiz_en: Spending a summer evening on the shores of Lake Gosho, what scenery would you most like to gaze at across the lake?

area_en: Morioka, Hanamaki, Kitakami, Ichinoseki, Oshu and Takizawa Cities, and nearby towns
desc_en: Rising in northern Iwate, this great river, representative of the Tohoku region, flows south through the center of the prefecture past Morioka, Hanamaki, Kitakami and Ichinoseki toward Miyagi Prefecture. Castle towns and the historic sites of Hiraizumi dot its basin, and history has grown up alongside the river. In central Morioka, the view of Mount Iwate across the river is beloved by residents.
quiz_en: Which Iwate-born poet wrote of the Kitakami River in the tanka beginning "Softly the willows turn green on the banks of the Kitakami..."?

desc_en: In Miyako City, this scenic spot woven from white rocks, green pines and clear blue sea represents the Sanriku Coast. Its name is said to come from its beauty being likened to the Pure Land paradise. In the calm cove you can tour among the rocks by sightseeing boat or small sappa boat, and in summer you can also enjoy swimming.
quiz_en: On the Jodogahama sightseeing boat, which seabirds fly right up close to the boat looking for food?

desc_en: The highest peak of the Kitakami Mountains has long been revered as a sacred mountain. It is made of a special rock called serpentinite, and precious alpine plants found nowhere else grow here. In the summer flower season many climbers visit to meet the delicate flowers blooming among the rocks. At its foot, Hayachine Kagura sacred dance has been passed down.
quiz_en: What is the name of the white flower, known as a relative of the edelweiss, that blooms only on Mount Hayachine?

desc_en: This highland lies in the Kitakami Mountains along the national highway linking Morioka and Miyako. Its high elevation keeps it cool even in summer, so many people stop to rest here while driving over the pass. Pastures and forests spread around it, and you can enjoy the grand scenery typical of the Kitakami Highlands, which changes with each season, from fresh green in early summer to autumn leaves.
quiz_en: At the Kuzakai Highlands on the road between Morioka and Miyako, what did you eat when you stopped to rest on your drive?

desc_en: This hot spring rises in Massaki, Ofunato City, near the Goishi Coast. The Goishi Coast, named for the round stones like go game pieces that cover its beach, is one of Sanriku's signature scenic spots. After exploring the coast with its sea cliffs and rocks carved by the waves, you can relax with seafood and hot springs at this seaside inn.
quiz_en: What color and shape are the stones covering the beach that gave the Goishi Coast, named after go game pieces, its name?

desc_en: This is the collective name for hot springs scattered in the hills west of Hanamaki City, offering a wide range of baths, from modern resorts to therapeutic spas along mountain streams. As befits Hanamaki, the hometown of Kenji Miyazawa, some people combine a visit with a tour of places associated with him. Each inn has distinctive baths waiting for you, including a deep rock bath you enter standing up.
quiz_en: What is the name of the famous rock bath at Namari Onsen in Hanamaki Onsen Village, so deep that you bathe standing up?

name_en: Cherry Blossoms of Kitakami Tenshochi Park
desc_en: This park spreads along the banks of the Kitakami River and is one of Tohoku's leading cherry blossom spots, with a long row of cherry trees lining the river. In full bloom, horse-drawn carriages slowly make their way beneath a tunnel of blossoms, and colorful koinobori (carp streamers) swim above the Kitakami River. From the observation deck you can take in the river, the cherries and distant mountains.
quiz_en: At the Tenshochi cherry blossom festival, what springtime tradition can be seen swimming in great numbers above the Kitakami River?

name_en: Geto Kogen Festival (Fresh Greenery and Autumn Leaves)
desc_en: This festival is held in the seasons of fresh greenery and autumn leaves at the Geto Kogen ski area in the Ou Mountains, west of Kitakami City. The highland, known in winter as a ski area with heavy snow, is wrapped in budding green from spring to early summer and in fiery autumn colors in fall. In the clear highland air, you can enjoy the seasonal colors of the mountains.
quiz_en: At the Geto Kogen festival in Kitakami, which would you rather see: the fresh green of spring or the fiery autumn leaves?

desc_en: This hot spring village rises along the Geto River, which flows deep in the Ou Mountains west of Kitakami City. In rustic open-air baths scattered along the riverbank, you can soak while hearing the murmur of the stream up close. The area receives heavy snow, and the valley wrapped in autumn leaves is exceptional. A simple atmosphere befitting a secret hot spring deep in the mountains still remains.
quiz_en: At Geto Kogen Onsen Village along the mountain stream, what scenery would you like to gaze at from an open-air bath right beside the river?

desc_en: This coast along the Pacific in Kuji City is lined with cliffs and strange rock formations. Kosode Coast is known for the "northernmost ama," women divers who catch sea urchins by free diving, and in summer you may be able to see a demonstration. Kuji became known nationwide as the setting of a TV drama and is also famous for producing amber. Rugged rocks and blue sea create a classic Sanriku landscape.
quiz_en: What was the 2013 NHK morning TV drama series modeled on the "northernmost ama" divers of Kosode Coast in Kuji City?

desc_en: This festival is held in early summer at the Hiraniwa Highlands in Yamagata, Kuji City, when the azaleas reach their peak. The highlands are known for beautiful birch forests, and the scene of vermilion azaleas spreading through the white-trunked woods and across the pastures is vivid. You can enjoy the flowers at a relaxed pace while feeling the cool breeze of these high-elevation highlands.
quiz_en: What is the name of the tree, famous at the Hiraniwa Highlands, that forms forests with beautiful rows of white trunks?

desc_en: This temple is in Matsuzaki, Tono City, known as the home of folktales. Trees grow thickly across its spacious grounds, and it is known as a spot where autumn leaves vividly color the precincts. Highlights, including a large Kannon statue, are scattered around, so you can stroll while feeling the changing seasons. Try visiting it along with Tono's rural scenery and places of legend.
quiz_en: What is the title of Kunio Yanagita's work that collected Tono's tales of kappa, zashiki-warashi and other legendary beings?

desc_en: This limestone cave in Higashiyama, Ichinoseki City, extends through extremely ancient rock layers. Inside, you can observe fossils of creatures that lived in the sea long ago and feel the long history of the Earth. In the cool air of the cave, you can enjoy an underground adventure while gazing at rock surfaces lit by lights.
quiz_en: What is the name of the gorge, also in Higashiyama, Ichinoseki City, where you can enjoy a boat ride while listening to boatmen's songs?

desc_en: This single-inn hot spring rises at a high elevation on the slopes of Mount Kurikoma, which straddles Iwate, Miyagi and Akita. Its abundant, strongly acidic water is milky white, and from the large open-air bath you can take in the mountain scenery. Marshes and ponds dot the surroundings, and in autumn the leaves coloring the mountainside are superb. It is also a busy base for climbers.
quiz_en: In the large open-air bath of Sukawa Kogen Onsen, which season would you choose: the autumn leaves or the fresh green?

desc_en: This volcano straddles three prefectures, Iwate, Miyagi and Akita, and on the Iwate side it is called Mount Sukawa. Marshes spread across its gentle summit area, with fields of alpine flowers in summer, and in autumn the whole mountain turns red and yellow, a sight praised as "the carpet of the gods." With well-maintained trails, it is a mountain beloved by many climbers.
quiz_en: This mountain is called "Sukawa-dake" on the Iwate side. By what name is it known on the Miyagi side?

desc_en: This mountain rises in eastern Ichinoseki City, near the border with Kesennuma City in Miyagi Prefecture. From near the summit, a grand panorama unfolds over the ridges of the Kitakami Mountains and, on clear days, all the way to the Pacific Ocean. It has long been a mountain of faith, with a shrine of distinguished history at its foot. On clear nights you can also enjoy a sky full of stars.
quiz_en: When you looked out over the Pacific Ocean from the summit of Mount Murone, what moved you the most?

desc_en: This port festival is held at Hirota Fishing Port on the Hirota Peninsula in Rikuzentakata City. Hirota Bay is a rich sea where oyster and scallop farming thrive, and the festival's events for tasting seafood are popular. Brimming with the energy of a fishing town, it lets you experience the strength of people who live with the sea and the cheerful bustle of a port town.
quiz_en: If you visited the Big Catch Festival on the Hirota Peninsula, which seafood from Hirota Bay would you most like to try?

name_en: Hikami and Amaterumioya Shrines Joint Grand Festival
desc_en: This grand festival is held jointly by Hikami Shrine and Amaterumioya Shrine in Takata, Rikuzentakata City, at fixed intervals of years. As a special ceremony not usually seen, the whole town joins in the preparations, and processions parade through the streets. For a town on the road to recovery from the earthquake disaster, it is an important event for reaffirming local bonds and traditions.
quiz_en: At Takata-Matsubara in Rikuzentakata, what is the pine tree called that survived the tsunami of the Great East Japan Earthquake?

desc_en: This gorge was carved through the hills by the Mabechi River, which flows through Ninohe City. Two great rocks called Ogami-iwa (Male God Rock) and Megami-iwa (Female God Rock) tower on opposite sides of the river, forming Ninohe's signature landscape. From the observatory you can take in the gorge and the town, and in the seasons of fresh green and autumn leaves the contrast between rock and trees is superb.
quiz_en: Of the two great rocks towering over Basenkyo Gorge, what is the name of the one that faces and pairs with Megami-iwa?

desc_en: This peaceful hot spring village spreads along the Mabechi River in Ninohe City. Long loved as a therapeutic spa, it has inns scattered through simple farmland. The village is known nationwide for an inn where a zashiki-warashi, a spirit in the form of a child, is said to appear, and some people come to stay hoping to meet it.
quiz_en: What is the child-like spirit said to appear at an inn in Kindaichi Onsen, bringing good fortune to those who meet it?

desc_en: This annual grand festival is held at Tendai-ji Temple in Joboji, Ninohe City. Affectionately known as "Katsura Shimizu," Tendai-ji is one of Tohoku's foremost historic temples; climb the long stone steps surrounded by cedar groves and the main hall stands quietly in the mountains. It is also known for having had the writer Jakucho Setouchi as its head priest, and many worshippers fill the grounds for the festival.
quiz_en: Who was the writer and Buddhist nun who served as head priest of Tendai-ji, drawing crowds from across Japan to her sermons?

desc_en: This mountain straddles Ninohe City, Karumai Town and Kunohe Village, and from near its summit you can look far out over the surrounding mountains. Its forest is known as one of Japan's leading habitats of the himebotaru, a tiny firefly, and on summer nights countless blinking lights fill the woods with a magical glow. It is a mountain with two faces: daytime views and nighttime lights.
quiz_en: On summer nights, what creature decorates the forests of Mount Orizume with countless tiny golden lights?

desc_en: Rising northwest of Morioka, this is the highest peak in Iwate Prefecture. Seen from Morioka, one side has a gentle slope, which earned it the name "Nanbu Kata-Fuji" (the one-sided Fuji of Nanbu), and residents cherish it as the home of their hearts. Takuboku Ishikawa and Kenji Miyazawa also loved this mountain. The shapes of lingering snow that appear on its slopes in early spring are a seasonal sign as well.
quiz_en: Seen from Morioka, one side of Mount Iwate slopes gently. What nickname was the mountain given because of that shape?

desc_en: This plateau with a gently rounded summit area spreads across the Iwate-Akita border. Marshes and ponds dot the Maries' fir forests, and the scenery changes with the seasons: alpine plants in summer, autumn leaves in fall and rime-covered trees in winter. Drive the Aspite Line mountain road and you will be greeted by magnificent views and mountain hot springs bubbling up here and there.
quiz_en: During the snowmelt season, what is the phenomenon called that appears on Kagami-numa pond at Hachimantai and looks like a giant eye?

desc_en: This hot spring village rises along the Matsukawa Gorge in the mountains of Hachimantai. Single inns proud of their milky-white sulfur springs are scattered here, retaining the charm of secret hot springs deep in the forest. Nearby is a power plant that uses geothermal heat, making this a place where you can feel the energy of the earth close at hand. In autumn the gorge is wrapped in fall colors.
quiz_en: What type of power plant, the first in Japan to begin full-scale commercial operation, is located near Matsukawa Onsen?

desc_en: This hot spring village is scattered across a highland resort area at the eastern foot of Hachimantai. Ski areas and hotels gather nearby, so you can enjoy hot springs after skiing in winter or in the cool highland breeze in summer. Its open scenery with Mount Iwate close at hand is a highlight, and it makes an ideal base for a trip around the Hachimantai mountains.
quiz_en: If you stayed overnight at Hachimantai Onsen Village, which famous spot around Hachimantai would you like to visit the next day?

desc_en: This hot spring lies in the hills of the Ashiro area of Hachimantai City, where the Appi River flows. The surroundings are a highland area known for skiing, including the Appi Kogen highlands, and bathing amid the snowy scenery is a winter treat. Wrapped in the quiet of a mountain village, you can warm up at leisure on a day trip or an overnight stay. It is also a good stop on the way back from skiing or a highland walk.
quiz_en: At Shin-Appi Onsen near the Appi Kogen highlands, what was the best part of soaking in the bath after a few ski runs?

desc_en: These are the remains of an ancient fortified government outpost built by Sakanoue no Tamuramaro at the beginning of the Heian period. Later, the Chinjufu, the military headquarters of Mutsu Province, was placed here, making it an important base for governing the Tohoku region. Today it is a spacious historic site that conveys how it once looked based on excavation findings. Amid the farmland of Mizusawa, you can reflect on the history of ancient Tohoku.
quiz_en: Who built Isawa Castle and is known as the shogun charged with subduing the north at the beginning of the Heian period?

desc_en: This historic Soto Zen temple in a mountain village of Mizusawa Ward, Oshu City, flourished as the center of the Soto school in the Tohoku region. Its main hall with an enormous thatched roof is a national Important Cultural Property, and its imposing form is breathtaking. The grounds, surrounded by cedar groves, are wrapped in stillness, and the thatched roof covered in snow in winter is also a magnificent sight.
quiz_en: The main hall of Shobo-ji has one of the largest roofs of its kind in Japan. What material is that huge roof made of?

desc_en: This mountain in Takizawa City rises as if nestled against the southeastern side of Mount Iwate. With well-maintained trails that let you reach the summit in a short time, it is popular with families and beginners. From the top you can take in the grand form of Mount Iwate looming right in front of you and the plains toward Morioka. There is also a campground at its foot for enjoying nature to the full.
quiz_en: Seeing Mount Iwate looming right in front of you from the summit of Mount Kurakake, what words slipped out of your mouth?

desc_en: This park is near Oshuku Onsen in Shizukuishi Town. A green spot typical of a mountain hot spring area, it is perfect for a walk between baths. Oshuku Onsen is a quiet hot spring town loved as a retreat for Morioka, with inns lining the river. You can spend peaceful time in the spa town while enjoying seasonal flowers and the greenery of the trees.
quiz_en: At Kotobuki Park near Oshuku Onsen, in which season would you most like to take a walk between hot spring baths?

name_en: Lake Gosho Regional Park Rides Plaza
desc_en: This plaza within the regional park on the shore of Lake Gosho offers rides for children. Amid the open lakeside scenery, it is a popular place for families to play and get moving. Lawns and walking paths surround it, and on clear days you can spend the whole day with views of Mount Iwate beyond the lake.
quiz_en: At the rides plaza in Lake Gosho Regional Park, if you could be a child again, which ride would you want to try?

desc_en: This festival celebrates the bounty of the farm at Kuzumaki Kogen Farm in Kuzumaki Town. Kuzumaki is a highland town where dairy farming thrives, known as "the town of milk, wine and clean energy." Its appeal is tasting dairy products and other flavors amid scenery of cows leisurely grazing on wide pastures.
quiz_en: What facilities line the highlands of Kuzumaki Town in a row, producing the town's clean energy?

desc_en: This hot spring is in the Ikatai area of Iwate Town. Iwate Town is a highland town north of Morioka, also known as the home of the source of the Kitakami River, the great river of the Tohoku region. In peaceful surroundings of fields and forests, take your time to enjoy the bath alongside local people, and then go and visit the beginning of the Kitakami River.
quiz_en: The Yuhazu Spring in Iwate Town is known as the source of which great river flowing through the Tohoku region?

desc_en: This hot spring village rises at the foot of the mountains in Yahaba Town, just south of Morioka. Close to central Morioka, it lets you casually enjoy a hot spring getaway in quiet surroundings backed by the Ou Mountains. Farmland spreads all around, and the scenery that changes with each season is another attraction. It is loved both as a base for sightseeing in Morioka and as a day-trip bath.
quiz_en: After soaking at Yahaba Onsen Village near Morioka, which local Morioka noodle dish would you like to eat?

desc_en: This is one of the hot springs of the Yuda Onsen gorge in Nishiwaga Town, near the Akita border. Nishiwaga is among Japan's snowiest areas, and in winter you can enjoy snow-viewing baths in a spa town wrapped in deep snow. On the Kitakami Line running through the town, there is even a station with a hot spring in its building, fitting for a hot spring village. It is a place to visit along with Lake Kinshu and its autumn leaves.
quiz_en: What is the name of the unique station in Nishiwaga Town on the Kitakami Line that has a hot spring facility inside the station building?

desc_en: This hot spring lies deep in the mountains of Nishiwaga Town, a quiet spa village that could be called the secluded inner retreat of the Yuda Onsen gorge. Inns line the mountain stream, surrounded by the deep forests of the Ou Mountains. Nishiwaga is known as a treasure trove of wild mountain vegetables, and tasting the mountain's bounty from spring to early summer is a pleasure. In snowy winter, its charm as a secret hot spring grows even stronger.
quiz_en: Which sticky wild mountain vegetable, picked in spring, is the most representative specialty of Nishiwaga, a treasure trove of wild greens?

desc_en: This hot spring lies in southern Nishiwaga Town, near the border with Akita Prefecture. Located along the national highway linking Iwate and Akita, it makes an easy stop on a trip across the prefectural border. The surroundings are a heavy-snow area enclosed by the Ou Mountains, turning into a silver world in winter. Soak in the stillness of the snowbound landscape and you will be warmed to the core.
quiz_en: At Sugo Onsen near the prefectural border, what scenery would you like to see out the window while soaking in the snowy season?

desc_en: This hot spring is in the Sawauchi area of Nishiwaga Town. Sawauchi is a snowy basin surrounded by the Ou Mountains, and it was once known for pioneering medical and welfare efforts to protect residents' lives. In calm surroundings of farmland and mountains, you can unwind slowly in a bath that is also loved by local people.
quiz_en: At Shigarai Onsen in the snowy Sawauchi basin, which would you choose: a snow-viewing bath in winter, or the season of fresh green?

desc_en: This quiet hot spring rises in the hills of Sawauchi, Nishiwaga Town, surrounded by the nature of the Ou Mountains. The area is a remote mountain region of spreading beech forests and also serves as a base for climbing into the Waga Mountains on the Akita border. It is cool in summer and wrapped in deep snow in winter, so you can spend calm, mountain-spa time throughout the four seasons.
quiz_en: What is the name of the mountain, known as the highest peak of the Waga Mountains, that rises to the west of the Sawauchi area?

desc_en: This hot spring lies in western Sawauchi, Nishiwaga Town, at the foot of a mountain rising on the Akita border. Surrounded by farmland and forest, you can soak at leisure while gazing at the mountain ridgeline. As befits snowy Nishiwaga, you can enjoy baths amid snowy scenery in winter, and from spring to autumn many people stop by on the way back from climbing or hiking.
quiz_en: What is the name of the mountain on the border of Nishiwaga Town and Akita Prefecture that also gives Mahiru Onsen its name?

desc_en: This chrysanthemum festival is held in autumn at Chuson-ji Temple in Hiraizumi, a World Heritage site. Carefully grown chrysanthemums line the grounds, adorning autumn in Hiraizumi along with the approach through cedar groves colored by autumn leaves. Chuson-ji is a temple associated with the Oshu Fujiwara clan, and its gleaming Konjikido (Golden Hall) conveys the Heian-period prayer for the Pure Land to the present day.
quiz_en: What is the Heian-period hall at Chuson-ji, covered inside and out with gold leaf, called?

desc_en: This festival is held in early summer at Motsu-ji Temple in Hiraizumi, a World Heritage site, when the flowers of its iris garden reach their peak. Motsu-ji preserves a Heian-period Pure Land garden centered on the Oizumi-ga-ike pond, and the sight of purple and white flowers adorning the pond's edge is elegance itself. Here you can sense the world of paradise that people of the Heian era envisioned.
quiz_en: At Motsu-ji's garden, what is the elegant event called in which people compose waka poems before a sake cup floating down a stream reaches them?

desc_en: This limestone cave in the mountains of Sumita Town is a rare place where a waterfall pours down deep inside. As you follow the cool passages through the cave, a waterfall appears with a roar, plunging forcefully from a crack in the rock, and its power will astonish you. It is a true cave-exploration experience where you can feel the force of water flowing underground.
quiz_en: What is the name of the waterfall that roars as it plunges down deep inside Rokando Cave?

desc_en: This waterfall is in the Namiita area of Otsuchi Town, near the Sanriku sea. It is a quiet spot surrounded by trees, where you can feel the clear flow of water heading from the mountains to the sea. The nearby Namiita Coast is known for distinctive waves that seem to come in without going back out, and surfing is enjoyed there. It is a place typical of Sanriku, where mountains and sea are close together.
quiz_en: What are the distinctive waves of Namiita Coast in Otsuchi Town called, said to "come in but never go back out"?

desc_en: This small island floating in Otsuchi Bay is striking, with a red lighthouse and a small shrine standing on it. Known as one of the models for the puppet show "Hyokkori Hyotanjima," it is beloved by local people. It was damaged by the tsunami of the Great East Japan Earthquake, but the lighthouse was rebuilt and has become a symbol of Otsuchi watching over the town's recovery.
quiz_en: What is the name of the NHK puppet show for which Horai Island is known as one of the models?

desc_en: This highland spreads across the border of Otsuchi Town and Tono City, an open place looking out over the ridges of the Kitakami Mountains. Large wind turbines line the ridge, letting you feel the strength of the wind sweeping across the pastures. On clear days you may even see the Pacific Ocean in the distance. It is a magnificent landscape well worth a drive.
quiz_en: When you looked up close at the large wind turbines lining the ridge of the Shinyama Highlands, what were your impressions?

desc_en: This festival of Yamada Hachimangu Shrine is held in autumn in Yamada, a port town on the Sanriku coast. Processions of mikoshi (portable shrines) and folk performing arts parade through town, and spirited shouts and drumbeats echo through the port. Yamada Bay is a calm bay where oyster and scallop farming thrive, and the festival season is also when autumn seafood becomes delicious.
quiz_en: Which shellfish, farmed widely in Yamada Bay and elsewhere in the Sanriku seas, is the classic in-shell favorite that comes into season in winter?

desc_en: One of Japan's foremost limestone caves, Ryusendo in Iwaizumi Town is designated a national Natural Monument. Inside are several highly transparent underground lakes, and the water lit by lights is a blue that seems to draw you in. This mysterious color is called "Dragon Blue." The water that springs from the cave is also known as famously pure water.
quiz_en: What is the name given to the clear blue color of the water that glows when lit in Ryusendo's underground lakes?

desc_en: This highland lies in the Kitakami Mountains along the road linking Iwaizumi Town and the Morioka area. Its high elevation brings cool breezes even in summer, and wide pastures and forests stretch on. Stop the car during a drive over the pass and a grand landscape typical of Iwate's deep mountains spreads before you, with the gentle ridges of the Kitakami Highlands layered one after another.
quiz_en: At the Hayasaka Highlands in the Kitakami Mountains, would you rather stop your car to see the view in the morning or at dusk?

desc_en: This park was developed at the Goshono Site in Ichinohe Town, the remains of a large Jomon-period settlement. Based on excavation findings, pit dwellings with earth-covered roofs and other structures have been reconstructed, letting you experience the scenery of a Jomon village. Surrounded by rich forest, it is registered as a World Heritage site as one of the Jomon Prehistoric Sites in Northern Japan, covering Hokkaido and northern Tohoku.
quiz_en: The pit dwellings reconstructed at Goshono Jomon Park have a distinctive roof covering. What material are their roofs covered with?

desc_en: This hot spring is in the Okunakayama Highlands of Ichinohe Town. Okunakayama is a highland area near the watershed between the Kitakami and Mabechi rivers, with pastoral scenery where dairy farming thrives. In winter the ski area is lively, and in summer the cool highland air is pleasant. It was once known as a difficult mountain pass for the railway and is a familiar place to train fans.
quiz_en: At Okunakayama, once a difficult stretch for the railway, what was the sight of three steam locomotives coupled together climbing the slope called?

desc_en: Held every year from August 6 to 8, this is one of Tohoku's representative summer festivals. Centered on Sendai's shopping streets, countless brilliantly colored streamers made of washi paper are hung up, turning the arcades into tunnels of light and color. It is a traditional event said to date back to the time of Date Masamune, and a fireworks display is held on the eve of the festival.
quiz_en: In the bamboo decorations of Sendai Tanabata, what are the gorgeous washi paper decorations that hang long beneath the kusudama balls called?

desc_en: This gorge near Naruko Onsen in Osaki City was carved deep by the Otani River. Sheer cliffs continue along both banks, and it is known as one of Tohoku's finest autumn foliage spots, turning red and yellow all over in fall. The view of the gorge from the observatory is spectacular, and a train running through the valley of autumn leaves is another highlight.
quiz_en: Amid the autumn leaves of Naruko Gorge, what is the name of the railway line whose trains pass over bridges and through tunnels?

name_en: Naruko Onsen: Katanuma Lake, Onsen Shrine and Takinoyu
desc_en: This is one of Tohoku's foremost hot spring areas in Osaki City, a spa town where many types of spring water bubble up. Takinoyu, the town's public bathhouse, is a historic bath that draws water from the spring at Onsen Shrine, and its wooden tubs create a charming atmosphere. Nearby Katanuma is a crater lake holding emerald-colored water. The town is also known for producing kokeshi dolls.
quiz_en: What is the traditional wooden doll, a Naruko Onsen specialty, that makes a squeaking "kyu-kyu" sound when you turn its head?

desc_en: In winter on the Zao mountain range, snow and ice carried by strong seasonal winds cover the trees, and giant rime-covered trees emerge. On the Miyagi side, tours that ride up to the fields of frosted trees in snow vehicles are popular. The scene of pure white, monster-like trees standing in rows is a winter work of art created by nature. On clear days, the contrast with the blue sky is superb.
quiz_en: At Miyagi Zao, what is the vehicle that moves over the snow on caterpillar tracks to take you to the fields of snow monsters?

desc_en: This historic Rinzai Zen temple by the sea at Matsushima is known as a temple that Date Masamune devoted great effort to rebuilding. Its main hall, a National Treasure, is a lavish building in the Momoyama style, and the sliding-door paintings and carvings inside are well worth seeing. Caves said to have been places of ascetic practice line the cedar-flanked approach, letting you feel the depth of history along with the Matsushima scenery.
quiz_en: Who was the first lord of the Sendai Domain, known for rebuilding Zuigan-ji into the form it has today?

desc_en: This scenic spot, where islands large and small float in Matsushima Bay, is counted among the Three Views of Japan. The scenery woven from pine-covered islands and rocks carved by the waves is classically viewed from a sightseeing boat. It is also a place Matsuo Basho visited in "The Narrow Road to the Deep North." Tasting grilled oysters at a seaside teahouse is another of Matsushima's pleasures.
quiz_en: Along with Amanohashidate in Kyoto and Miyajima in Hiroshima, Matsushima is one of a famous trio of scenic spots. What is this trio called?

name_en: East Gate of the Outer Wall, Akita Castle Ruins
