desc_en: These are the remains of Akita Castle, an ancient fortified outpost built in the Nara period and placed as the northern base on the Sea of Japan side. Based on excavations, the east gate of the outer enclosure and its earthen walls have been reconstructed, letting you see how it once looked. Rare remains that tell of daily life at the time have also been found, making this a place to feel the history of exchange between ancient Tohoku and the Asian continent.
quiz_en: A rare toilet structure believed to date from the Nara period was found at the Akita Castle Ruins. What type of toilet was it?

desc_en: This festival at Hoshitsuji Shrine in Omachi, Akita City, is devoted to daruma, the lucky dolls. Daruma of all sizes line the in-town shrine, which bustles with people praying for good health and business prosperity in the year ahead. In the snowy season in Akita, the red of the daruma stands out vividly. You can enjoy the atmosphere of an old-fashioned shrine fair.
quiz_en: At the Daruma Festival of Hoshitsuji Shrine, what wish for this year would you like to place in your daruma doll?

desc_en: At this festival, people dance to "Taishoji Okesa," a folk song handed down in the Taishoji area of Yuwa, Akita City. Local residents carefully carry on this song and dance rooted in their community, dancing in a circle on summer nights. Singing and festival music echo through the peaceful countryside, and you can feel the warm ties among the local people.
quiz_en: What is the name of the major river representative of Akita Prefecture that flows through the Yuwa area and into the Sea of Japan at Akita City?

desc_en: This hot spring rises along the upper Iwami River in the hills of Kawabe, Akita City. Although it is within driving distance of central Akita, it is a quiet mountain village surrounded by deep greenery. There is also a scenic gorge along the nearby Iwami River, so in the seasons of fresh green and autumn leaves you can combine a riverside walk with a relaxing time at this mountain spa.
quiz_en: At Iwami Onsen, a secluded retreat of Akita City, which season would be best for a walk along the river after your bath?

desc_en: This hot spring rises at the foot of Mount Taiheizan in the Taihei area of Akita City. Mount Taiheizan is a sacred mountain rising east of Akita City and has long been beloved by residents. Farmland and forest spread around it, and you can soak at leisure in the clear mountain air. It is perfect for stopping by to wash off the sweat on the way back from climbing or hiking.
quiz_en: After a soak at Kainosawa Onsen, would you rather climb sacred Mount Taiheizan or stroll through the farmland around its foot?

name_en: Kiritanpo Hot Pot of Northern Akita
desc_en: This signature Akita hot pot dish features "kiritanpo," cooked rice mashed, wrapped around cedar sticks and grilled, simmered in a soup rich with chicken stock. The northern part of the prefecture, such as Kazuno and Odate, is known as its birthplace. Enjoyed with burdock, maitake mushrooms, Japanese parsley and other ingredients, it is a taste of the season from the new rice harvest through winter.
quiz_en: What is the name of Akita's signature brand of local chicken, essential for the broth of kiritanpo hot pot?

name_en: Beech Forests of the Shirakami Mountains (Akita Side)
desc_en: The Shirakami Mountains, spreading across the Akita-Aomori border, are a World Natural Heritage site where vast virgin beech forests untouched by human hands remain. You can also enter the forest from the Akita side, around Fujisato and Happo towns, and walking among the towering giant trees lets you feel the richness of a beech forest that nurtures many living things. In autumn the whole forest glows gold.
quiz_en: What is the name of the large woodpecker with a black body and striking red head that lives in the beech forests of Shirakami?

name_en: Ichozan Shrine and Nanakura Tenmangu Shrine
desc_en: These shrines sit in the hills along the Yoneshiro River in Futatsui, Noshiro City. Futatsui is a scenic area where the Yoneshiro River winds among the mountains, with the greenery of Mount Nanakura pressing close along the river. The grounds, surrounded by quiet forest, feel refreshing, and in autumn the trees take on color and adorn the precincts. These shrines are embraced by the flow of the Yoneshiro River and mountain nature.
quiz_en: What is the scenic spot along the Yoneshiro River in Futatsui, known by a name connected to an imperial tour by Emperor Meiji?

desc_en: This park with a long row of cherry trees lies on the banks of the Yoneshiro River, which flows through Noshiro City. In spring the riverside embankment turns cherry-pink, and you can enjoy viewing the blossoms while feeling the breeze blowing across the water. Noshiro prospered as a lumber town facing the Sea of Japan and is also known nationwide for a powerhouse high school basketball team.
quiz_en: Because it is home to a powerhouse high school basketball team, Noshiro City is known as the city of what?

desc_en: This festival at Okihake Shrine in Hiraka, Yokote City, is devoted to the Teashi (Hands and Feet) Kannon. It draws the faith of people who pray for healthy hands and feet and has been carefully carried on by the local community. Located in the farmland of the Yokote Basin, the shrine welcomes worshippers from nearby on festival day, wrapped in the simple, peaceful atmosphere of a village festival.
quiz_en: If you visited the Teashi Kannon festival to pray, whose hands and feet would you wish good health for?

desc_en: This Hatsuuma festival is held at Kido Gorobe Shrine in Numadate, Omonogawa, Yokote City. Hatsuuma is an observance tied to Inari worship and is carried on in many places as a festival praying for bountiful harvests and business prosperity. Held in winter in the snowy Yokote Basin, it is an important occasion for local people to gather and pray for the coming of spring and the year's harvest.
quiz_en: The Hatsuuma festival is generally held on the first "Day of the Horse" of which month in the traditional calendar?

desc_en: This cherry blossom festival is held in spring at Yokote Park, the site of Yokote Castle. On the hilltop stands an observatory modeled on a castle keep, so you can enjoy cherries in full bloom together with the castle. From the observatory you can take in central Yokote, the Yokote Basin and the Ou Mountains. Yokote, known for its winter kamakura, is wrapped in cherry-pink in spring.
quiz_en: In Yokote's Little New Year event, children gather inside snow huts where the water god is enshrined. What are these snow huts called?

desc_en: This park in the hills of the Kanazawa area of Yokote City is a historic place said to be the site of a fortified stockade that was the stage of a battle in the late Heian period. Hachiman Shrine stands within the park, and you can stroll while sensing traces of the old battlefield. Spring cherry blossoms and autumn leaves are also beautiful, and from the heights you can look out over the wide farmland of the Yokote Basin.
quiz_en: What is the late Heian-period war fought by Minamoto no Yoshiie, said to have taken place around Kanazawa Park, called?

desc_en: At this festival at Sansho Shrine in Masuda, Yokote City, bonten are offered to the shrine. Bonten are large pillar-like offerings adorned with colorful decorations, and young men carry them spiritedly to the shrine. Masuda is a historic town where streets of kura storehouses remain, and the shouts echoing through the snowy winter bring the town to life.
quiz_en: What are the storehouses called, found in many Masuda homes, that were built inside the main house and carefully protected?

desc_en: This cherry blossom festival is held at Manto Park in Masuda, Yokote City. The park, spreading at the foot of Mount Manto, is planted with many cherry trees and bustles with people enjoying the blossoms beside the pond and the cherries lit up at night. Masuda is an area where fruit growing thrives, with apple orchards around it, creating a peaceful scene befitting a village of flowers in spring.
quiz_en: At the Manto Park Cherry Blossom Festival, which would you rather enjoy: cherries under a blue daytime sky, or blossoms at night?

desc_en: These castle ruins are in Kamiyoshida, Hiraka, Yokote City. Located on the plains of the Yokote Basin, the site is surrounded by wide farmland. It conveys the history of the people who once ruled this area, and as you stand at the quiet historic site, you can imagine the basin in the age of the warring states. The rice paddy scenery through the four seasons is another attraction.
quiz_en: At the Yoshida Castle Ruins amid the farmland of the Yokote Basin, in which season of rice paddies would you like to view the site?

desc_en: This pond is in Asamai, Hiraka, Yokote City. The Yokote Basin is a land blessed with water, where water from the Ou Mountains travels underground and springs to the surface. The pondside is a quiet waterside space, a place for local people to stroll and relax. You can spend a leisurely time gazing at the sky reflected on the water and the surrounding greenery.
quiz_en: If you walked along the shore of Biwa-numa, a waterside spot in the Yokote Basin, what creatures would you like to encounter?

desc_en: This shrine is in Imajuku, Omonogawa, Yokote City. It stands in the farmland along the Omono River and has been cared for by local people. The wide rice paddies of the Yokote Basin spread around it, and the shrine standing amid scenery that turns green or gold with the seasons lets you feel the bond between village life and faith.
quiz_en: Have you ever asked local people about the origin of the name of Kubizuka Shrine, standing in the farmland of the Omono River basin?

desc_en: This is the kagura hall of Hojiwake Shrine in Omori, Yokote City, which has been the center of faith in Mount Horowa. As a building that preserves an architectural style from early times, it is designated a national Important Cultural Property. Kagura sacred dance has been handed down at this shrine since long ago, and in its quiet mountain-village grounds you can encounter a faith nurtured over a long history.
quiz_en: What is the name of the mountain in Omori, Yokote City, at the center of the faith of Hojiwake Shrine?

desc_en: This park in Jumonji, Yokote City, is loved as a place for local people to relax. Jumonji is a town in the southern part of the Yokote Basin, famous for its light chuka soba (ramen) made with dried sardine broth. After enjoying the seasonal flowers and greenery of the park, it is a good idea to taste an old-fashioned bowl at a local diner.
quiz_en: What slightly unusual topping is found in "Jumonji chuka soba," the local ramen of Jumonji in Yokote City?

desc_en: This hot spring is in the hills of the Sannai area of Yokote City. Sannai is an area rich in nature, embraced by the Ou Mountains, and known for its specialty taro, "Sannai imonoko." In autumn you may see people gathered around pots of imonoko-jiru taro soup, in a land blessed with mountain bounty. Soak in the quiet hot spring and relax with the flavors of the mountain village.
quiz_en: What is the name of the sticky taro, a Sannai specialty, that is essential for the autumn taro soup imonoko-jiru?

desc_en: This park in the Taiyu area of Yokote City has cherry trees planted along a riverside embankment. In spring a row of cherry trees continues on and on, creating a ribbon of flowers through the peaceful farmland. The surrounding Yokote Basin is a rich rice-growing region. After viewing the blossoms, why not try the famous Yokote yakisoba, with thick noodles, sweetish sauce and a fried egg on top?
quiz_en: As a topping on the local specialty Yokote yakisoba, what egg dish is placed on top of the noodles?

desc_en: This hot spring rises along the Yoneshiro River in Juniso, Odate City. It is a historic spa town long used for therapeutic bathing, retaining a calm riverside atmosphere. Odate is known as the home of the Akita dog, and the faithful dog Hachiko, who kept waiting for his master in Shibuya, was born here. You can enjoy the town of Akita dogs along with the hot springs.
quiz_en: What is the name of the Akita dog born in Odate City, famous for waiting for his master's return at Shibuya Station?

desc_en: This hot spring spreads along a deep V-shaped gorge carved by the Minase River in Minase, Yuzawa City. Boiling water and steam spurt forcefully from cracks in the gorge's rocks, and a walking path down to the valley floor lets you see their power up close. In autumn the gorge is wrapped in fall colors, and the combination of rising steam and colorful trees creates a superb view.
quiz_en: At Oyasukyo, what is the spot called where boiling water and steam spurt forcefully from cracks in the rocks of the gorge?

desc_en: This hot spring sits quietly deep in the mountains of Takamatsu, Yuzawa City, in a valley where volcanic fumes rise. As its name, meaning "mud hot water," suggests, it is known for gray, muddy spring water, and the rugged terrain and rising steam around it create the feel of a hidden hot spring. Nearby there is also a sulfurous fumarole area where no plants grow, a place to feel the power of the earth.
quiz_en: What is the name of the desolate sacred site near Doroyu Onsen, where no plants grow and sulfurous fumes hang in the air?

desc_en: This hot spring is in the Kijiyama Highlands of Takamatsu, Yuzawa City. Kijiyama is an area where kijishi, woodturners, have lived since long ago, and it is known for producing traditional kokeshi dolls with simple, rustic expressions. In quiet surroundings of clear highland air and forest, you can relax while soaking in the bath. Autumn is a beautiful season, with the surrounding mountains in fall colors.
quiz_en: In the Kijiyama area of Yuzawa City, what traditional wooden doll have woodturners continued to make for generations?

name_en: Goshogake Onsen: Mud Volcanoes and Traditional Healing Baths
desc_en: This therapeutic spa inn lies in the mountains of Hachimantai, surrounded by mud volcanoes where mud bubbles up and by steaming vents. Traditional healing culture is still alive here, such as the box steam bath, where you sit in a box with only your head outside and warm up in the steam, and ondol rooms with floors heated by geothermal warmth. Walking the nature trail, you can feel the pulse of the earth up close.
quiz_en: There is a saying, "Come to Goshogake on a horse, go home in wooden clogs." What quality of this hot spring does it describe?

desc_en: This hot spring village rises along the Yoneshiro River gorge in Hachimantai, Kazuno City. Its name is said to come from hot water that once bubbled up from the river's shallows, and it is a calm spa town with inns lining the river. Hanawa Line trains run along the gorge, and in autumn the valley is wrapped in fall colors. It is also a convenient base for trips to Hachimantai and Lake Towada.
quiz_en: What is the name of the summer festival in Kazuno City, a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, in which lavish floats parade through town?

desc_en: This hot spring village spreads along the Oyu River in Towada-Oyu, Kazuno City. It is a historic hot spring that has long flourished as a therapeutic spa, and the town has public bathhouses, so hopping between baths is part of the fun. Nearby are large Jomon-period stone circles, and the chance to enjoy World Heritage Jomon sites together with hot springs is a charm unique to this place.
quiz_en: What is the site near Oyu Onsen called, where stones were arranged in circles during the Jomon period?

desc_en: This is the site of a mine with a long history in Kazuno City. Until it closed in the Showa era, large amounts of ore were dug out here, supporting the region's development. Today part of the mine tunnels is open to visitors, and as you walk through the cool shafts, you can learn about past mining methods and the lives of the people who worked in the mine.
quiz_en: What reddish metal, also used in electric wires and cables, was mainly mined at the Osarizawa Mine?

desc_en: Rising on the border of Akita and Yamagata, this is one of Tohoku's highest peaks, a beautiful solitary mountain that rises straight up from the Sea of Japan. In various places it is called by nicknames bearing the name "Fuji," and snow lingering near the summit and alpine plants in summer captivate climbers. Its snowmelt becomes abundant underground water that nourishes the fields and sea at its foot.
quiz_en: In Akita, Mount Chokai is called "Akita Fuji." By what name is it known on the Yamagata Prefecture side?

desc_en: This gorge runs through the hills of Oyana, Yurihonjo City. In the valley carved through the mountains by the river, a clear stream flows on, and a quiet landscape of rocks and trees unfolds. It is wrapped in fresh, vivid green in early summer and autumn colors in fall, and walking along the stream you will be soothed by the sound of water and the mountain air. It is a place to feel the nature of Yurihonjo.
quiz_en: Walking along the stream at Ishizawa Gorge in the hills of Yurihonjo, what sound stayed with you the most?

desc_en: This hot spring is in central Yurihonjo City, where you can casually enjoy a bath right in town. Honjo is a castle town that developed near the mouth of the Koyoshi River, with calm streets spreading along the river. Its appeal is the convenience of stopping by between walks and sightseeing, and after easing your travel fatigue, head into town to taste seafood from the Sea of Japan.
quiz_en: What is the name of the river that flows through the center of Yurihonjo City and empties into the Sea of Japan?

desc_en: This castle-shaped facility stands on a hill overlooking the Sea of Japan in Iwaki, Yurihonjo City. Iwaki once prospered as the castle town of the Kameda Domain, and from the hill there are broad views over the Sea of Japan. At dusk on a clear day, the sun sinking into the sea colors the sky and water in a spectacular view. It is a place to enjoy history and sea views together.
quiz_en: At Tensagi Wine Castle overlooking the Sea of Japan, what color of sky would you most like to see at dusk?

desc_en: This festival is held on the Yurihara Highlands at the northern foot of Mount Chokai. Yurihara is a gently rolling plateau of pastures and fields, and the sight of Mount Chokai rising majestically before you is breathtaking. As the cool highland breeze blows through, you can enjoy the festival events while fully taking in the scenery of the grand mountain and wide sky.
quiz_en: At the festival on the Yurihara Highlands, what photo would you like to take with Mount Chokai towering behind you?

desc_en: This hot spring is in Nishime, Yurihonjo City. Nishime is a farming town near the Sea of Japan with peaceful village scenery. After warming up in a bath loved by local people, head a little farther to the Sea of Japan coast. On clear days you can see Mount Chokai to the south, and at dusk you can also enjoy the sun setting into the sea.
quiz_en: After a soak at Kashiwa Onsen in Nishime near the Sea of Japan, which would you rather see: Mount Chokai or a sunset over the sea?

desc_en: This hot spring lies in the hills of Yunosawa in the Taki area of Yurihonjo City. Surrounded by the nature of the countryside, you can soak quietly while feeling the changing seasons. Its charm is a simple, calm atmosphere quite different from a busy spa town. It is recommended for those who want to spend unhurried time while experiencing mountain-village life in the Yuri region.
quiz_en: At Taki Onsen in the hills of Yurihonjo, what did you hear when you listened carefully while soaking in the quiet bath?

desc_en: This hot spring is in the farmland along the Omono River in western Daisen City. The inn stands amid gentle scenery where the river makes great bends, and you can enjoy the bath wrapped in the peaceful air of the countryside. Its charm is spending calm time watching the river flow. The somewhat tricky-to-read place name also sticks in the memory.
quiz_en: At Kowakubi Onsen beside the great bends of the Omono River, how would you like to spend a calm afternoon watching the water flow?

desc_en: This hot spring is in the farmland spreading at the foot of the Ou Mountains in Ota, Daisen City. The wide rice paddies of the Senboku Plain continue all around, creating a peaceful scene together with the mountains behind. Daisen City is known nationwide for its summer fireworks competition, and in this bath close to local people's daily lives, you can rest your body at leisure.
quiz_en: What is the popular name of the fireworks competition held every summer in Daisen City, where pyrotechnicians from all over Japan compete?

desc_en: This annual grand festival is held in summer at Hachimangu Tsuzureko Shrine in Tsuzureko, Kitaakita City. The star of the festival is a giant drum whose diameter far exceeds a person's height. Its deep bass booms right through to your gut, overwhelming the many spectators. It is a festival that heats up summer in Kitaakita, carried on with pride by local people.
quiz_en: What is the giant musical instrument, recognized by Guinness World Records, that is played at the Tsuzureko Shrine annual festival?

desc_en: This hot spring lies in the hills of Komori, Kitaakita City. Kitaakita embraces a rich mountain region, including Mount Moriyoshi, and in winter you can see magical scenery where snow and ice cover the trees. In the quiet of the deep mountains, you can take a leisurely soak in a bath loved by local people and feel the blessings of Kitaakita's nature.
quiz_en: What natural formations, created when snow and ice completely cover the trees, can be seen on Mount Moriyoshi in Kitaakita in winter?

desc_en: This hot spring is in Utto, Ani, Kitaakita City, a village of the Matagi deep in the mountains. The Ani region is known as a land where the culture of the Matagi, traditional hunters who hunt while revering the mountain gods, has been handed down. Nearby there are also facilities introducing the Matagi way of life, and you can experience this unique culture along with dishes that make use of the mountain's bounty.
quiz_en: What are the traditional hunters of the Ani region called, who hunt in groups while revering the mountain gods?

desc_en: This waterfall in the hills of Kisakata, Nikaho City, flows down in many streams that seem to spring out from between moss-covered rocks. The water is underground water from snow and rain that fell on Mount Chokai and passed through the earth over many years, and the air around it stays cool even in summer. The scenery created by green moss and streams of white water is mystical.
quiz_en: The underground water springing from the mossy rocks of Mototaki Falls originally fell as snow and rain on which mountain?

desc_en: This waterfall is within the grounds of Kinpo Shrine in Kisakata, Nikaho City, and is designated a national Place of Scenic Beauty. The Naso River, gathering snowmelt from Mount Chokai, pours down the rock wall like a sheet of white cloth in a splendid sight. As you descend the stone steps to the plunge pool, spray and a thundering roar close in. Kisakata was once a scenic inlet dotted with islands.
quiz_en: What is the title of Matsuo Basho's travel journal recording his visit to Kisakata, once an inlet dotted with islands?

desc_en: This hot spring in the mountains on the western side of Hachimantai is known for its strongly acidic water. A huge amount of boiling water gushes from its source, and in the surrounding geothermal area you can see people warming themselves on straw mats spread over the bedrock. A rare mineral designated a Special Natural Monument is also found here, and many people visit from all over Japan for therapeutic bathing.
quiz_en: What is the mineral found at Tamagawa Onsen, designated a Special Natural Monument and known for containing radium?

desc_en: This hot spring village at the foot of Mount Nyuto has distinctive single inns scattered through the beech forest. Each inn has its own spring source, so as you hop between baths you can enjoy the differences, from milky white water to clear water. The scenery of old thatched-roof spa inns looks just like a world from a folktale. Open-air baths in deep winter snow have a special charm too.
quiz_en: Which inn is said to have the oldest history in Nyuto Onsen Village, known for its thatched row house and milky open-air bath?

desc_en: This hot spring area spreads across the plateau between Lake Tazawa and Mount Akita-Komagatake in Tazawako, Semboku City. It is a highland resort with ski areas, hotels and guesthouses, busy in winter with skiing and in summer as a base for climbing and hiking. The view looking down on Lake Tazawa from the highlands is also lovely, and you can enjoy mountain hot springs and cool highland breezes.
quiz_en: What is the name of the mountain that rises above the Tazawako Highlands and is known in summer as a treasure trove of alpine plants?

desc_en: This festival is held during the autumn foliage season at Dakigaeri Gorge in Tazawako, Semboku City. In the gorge carved by the Tama River, a crystal-clear cobalt-blue stream and sheer rock walls continue on, and the color contrast with red and yellow autumn leaves is superb. Cross the suspension bridge and walk the trail along the gorge, and a stunning view typical of autumn in Tohoku unfolds.
quiz_en: What is the waterfall at the end of the Dakigaeri Gorge trail, said to be named for being so beautiful that people turn back to look?

desc_en: This nearly circular lake is known as the deepest lake in Japan. Its water holds a deep lapis-lazuli blue, and it is known for not freezing over even in winter. On the shore stands a golden statue modeled on a legendary princess who is said to have become a dragon in her wish for eternal beauty, creating a striking contrast with the lake's blue. A drive around the lake is also recommended.
quiz_en: The golden statue on the shore of Lake Tazawa depicts a princess from the lake's legend. What is her name?

desc_en: This is the lakeshore on the Kosaka Town side, Akita Prefecture, of Lake Towada, which straddles the border with Aomori. From the Hakka Pass observatory overlooking the lake, a grand view unfolds of the lake and peninsulas surrounded by the outer caldera rim. Himemasu (kokanee salmon) have been released into the lake and can be enjoyed as a local specialty. The lake wrapped in autumn leaves is exceptional.
quiz_en: Who is the person known for succeeding, after great hardship, in farming himemasu kokanee salmon in Lake Towada?
